title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (§ on the 'équation des lacets', continuing pp. ~313-315). Let D be the Poincaré upper half-plane and pi(2) = Gamma(2) the kernel of SL(2,Z) -> SL(2,Z/2Z) ≅ S_3. Modulo ±1, Gamma(2) is free of rank 2 and is identified with pi_{0,3}. Then U_{0,3}^an = P^1 - {0,1,∞} ≅ D/Gamma(2), via the Legendre lambda-function. To make D the universal cover of U_{0,3} pointed at a chosen point, one must fix a point of D above the base point.

The chosen base points of U_{0,3} are the two fixed points P, P̄ of the S_3-action on the lambda-line, i.e. lambda = e^{±i pi/3} (written P = -j̄, P̄ = -j). Upstairs one takes J = e^{2 i pi/3} and -J̄ = e^{i pi/3}.

The previous page shows that the elements of SL(2,Z) (mod ±1) sending J to -J̄ are (1 1;0 1), (1 0;1 1) and (0 -1;1 0). None of them is ≡ Id mod 2, so J and -J̄ are not Gamma(2)-congruent. Hence their images in D/pi(2) are the two distinct points P and P̄ (in some order).

The bracket closes with the conclusion: the lift of P is characterized by tau ∈ D being a root of unity, 'which is quite natural'. With this choice the homomorphism (73) is 'normalised' into an effective homomorphism, and the same holds for (70).

Grothendieck then states a wish: redo the preceding constructions in the profinite setting. He lacks the foundations, above all a theory of 'tronçons' ('jonglage de tours') at the level of profinite 'groupes à lacets'. The next page says this would give a 'gruppentheoretisch' understanding of a homomorphism from the profinite object attached to (0,3) to GL(2,Ẑ)/±1. That is the main motivation of the §. He anticipates that the profinite extension may require extra arithmetic structure: a subgroup Pi ⊂ Autext_lac(pi_{0,3}^) subject to 'exponential'-type relations, which is essentially the GT-type set-up.
errors: No mathematical error. The non-congruence argument is correct: the elements sending J to -J̄ form one coset g·Stab(J), of size 3 mod ±1, and the three listed matrices are exactly that coset, none ≡ Id mod 2. The characterization is also correct and unique: within the Gamma(2)-orbit of J, J is the only root of unity, since the only roots of unity in the SL(2,Z)-orbit of J are J and -J̄, and these are not Gamma(2)-equivalent. Gap: the exact matching P versus P̄ is left 'ou inversement', i.e. which of lambda(J), lambda(-J̄) is e^{i pi/3} is not settled on the page.

ideas.what: Uniformization U_{0,3}^an ≅ D/Gamma(2) with pi_{0,3} ≅ Gamma(2)/±1. Base points taken at the S_3-fixed points e^{±i pi/3}, lifted to the root of unity e^{2 i pi/3} in D.
ideas.modern_name: Legendre lambda-uniformization; tangential/symmetric base points at the S_3-fixed points of the lambda-line
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Legendre/Jacobi/Klein); use of symmetric base points appears in Ihara, Nakamura and others

ideas.what: Normalising an outer homomorphism into an actual ('effective') homomorphism by a canonical choice of base point (the root-of-unity lift).
ideas.modern_name: Lifting outer actions to genuine actions via a rigid base point
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard technique in anabelian/GT literature (Ihara, Nakamura)

ideas.what: Programme to transfer the 'tronçon' / tower-juggling constructions to profinite loop groups, possibly needing a subgroup Pi of Autext_lac(pi_{0,3}^) defined by exponential-type relations.
ideas.modern_name: Profinite Teichmüller tower; Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT^ defined by Drinfeld-type relations
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un Programme (1984), §2 on the Teichmüller tower and two-level generation

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly records the absence of a profinite theory of 'tronçons' for loop groups as the obstacle to a group-theoretic understanding of the map to GL(2,Ẑ)/±1. He also anticipates that extra arithmetic structure (a subgroup of Autext_lac with exponential-type relations) is needed. This thread was later realised by the GT literature, so it is a historical precursor rather than an open gap.
missed.quote: malheureusement je manque des fondements nécessaires, et surtout d'une théorie des "tronçons" — "jonglage de tours" au niveau groupes à lacets profinis
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents that, around the Longue Marche period, Grothendieck anticipated the need for GT-like relations before Drinfeld. This is of historical interest; the mathematics is now covered by GT and genus-one GT work (Nakamura, Schneps, Enriquez).

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly routine: classical lambda-uniformization and a careful base-point choice. The profinite wish is a known theme of the Esquisse and was later carried out (Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps). The anticipation of relation-defined subgroups of Autext_lac is a mildly notable pre-GT detail.
transcription_corrections: 'P = -j et P̄ = -j̄' should read 'P = -j̄ et P̄ = -j (ou inversement)', consistent with the previous page's P = -J̄.
'de ce qu'ils sont pas [?] = image' is uncertain; likely 'de ce qu'ils n'ont pas même image dans U_{0,3}^an'.
'et donc en conséquence [?] (70)' likely reads 'et de même aussi (70)'.
'est [-été-]' is probably a deleted 'donc' or 'dit'; the struck word before 'une racine de l'unité' is illegible.
